Morey is the sole listed sponsor of HB 278, Protect Military Votes. The bill's title says it would write into law a State Board of Elections rule that overseas and military voters casting a military-overseas ballot do not have to include photo identification. Bill text: 'A covered voter voting under this Article shall not be required to include a photocopy of identification described in G.S. 163-166.16(a) or an affidavit as described in G.S. 163-166.16(d)(1), (d)(2), or (d)(3) when submitting a ballot in accordance with this Article.' Referred to committee; no further action shown on the member page. Date is the filing date shown on the member's introduced-bills page.
subjects: photo ID for military and overseas ballots

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, Second Reading
findings.note: Morey voted no on second reading of HB 958 (66 aye, 47 no on the roll call for the whole House). Bill text (ratified version, https://www.ncleg.gov/Sessions/2025/Bills/House/PDF/H958v9.pdf) includes: DMV staff proceed with a voter registration only if the applicant affirmatively states US citizenship; county boards process a registration only if it affirmatively indicates citizenship, with a sworn citizenship statement if the answer is blank; and a State Board process to remove potential non-citizens flagged from a federal database. It also covers removal of deceased voters, absentee-ballot challenges and campaign finance.

findings.motion: HB 958 Election Law Changes, M11 Concur (House vote on the Senate changes)
findings.note: Morey voted no on the motion to concur in the Senate version of HB 958, which passed the House 62 to 47. The ratified text includes the citizenship-on-registration rules and the non-citizen voter-removal process described above.
